---
title: "lfpack"
subtitle: "Lossy LFP codec for Neuropixels recordings"
---

**lfpack** compresses Neuropixels LFP into random-access HDF5 files of about **1.5 %** of the
decimated (250 Hz, float32) data, and reads them back through a drop-in replacement for
`spikeglx.Reader`. The raw band is cleaned, decimated to 250 Hz and denoised, then every 8 s
chunk is coded as an SVD whose spatial modes live in one shared basis per recording and whose
temporal modes are thresholded wavelet packets.

```bash
pip install lfpack
```

```python
from lfpack import compress_bin_to_h5, LFPackReader

compress_bin_to_h5("recording.lf.cbin", "recording.lf.h5")

sr = LFPackReader("recording.lf.h5")
traces = sr[0:1000]      # (1000, n_channels) float32, volts
```

## Choosing α

α, the wavelet-packet threshold, is the only parameter that moves behaviour decoding
(11 IBL NP1 recordings, ε = 100, shared basis of 32 vectors):

| α | file / 250 Hz float32 | SNR | wheel-speed R² below uncompressed (mean) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 14 | 0.82 % | 14.4 dB | 0.0054 |
| **7 (default)** | **1.55 %** | **18.5 dB** | **0.0030** |
| 2.5 | 3.09 % | 23.4 dB | 0.0005 |

See [the codec](explanation/pipeline.qmd#codec) for how these were measured.
